question: Does the packet3 shared4_row64 planar-Q6 owner also win, bit-exactly, on the two remaining staged-cycle planar shapes (attention_v and recurrent_qkv) at every row 1-128?
method: scripts/qwen38_packet3_q6_planar_wmma_row_leaf.py --shapes attention_v,recurrent_qkv; one-wave parent vs shared4_row64 on identical repacked tiles + BF16 activations; event-timed medians of 3 bursts of 16 after 4 warmups; outputs compared bit-exactly vs the parent per row
decision: attention_v (5120->1024): bit-exact at EVERY screened row 1-128 (0 mismatches) and faster at every row, 1.22-2.64x overall and 1.22-2.0x across the staged verify-frontier rows 4-36; band admitted rows 4-128 -> shared4_row64 (rows >=129 stay on the parent pending a shared4 screen at this shape). recurrent_qkv (5120->10240): bit-exact everywhere but flat (0.92-1.09x at cycle rows) - rejected, parent retained.
limitations: Rows >=129 for attention_v are unscreened for the shared4 (256-row) owner at this shape and stay on the one-wave parent.
Standalone leaf timings; cycle-level proof is the retained nine-cell sweep on the band commit.
recurrent_qkv rejection is a measured no-win at cycle rows, not a correctness finding.
